drivers.label: AI semiconductor revenue (custom XPUs + AI networking)
drivers.source: Actuals from Broadcom's quarterly releases (8-K Ex.99.1, source ids 60-66): Q1 FY25 $4.1B, Q2 'over $4.4B', Q3 $5.2B, Q1 FY26 $8.4B, Q2 FY26 $10.8B, Q3 FY26 $16.7B; Q4 FY25 6,460 derived from the Q3 FY26 release (Q4 FY26 guide $21.7B 'up 236% year-over-year' -> 21.7 / 3.36 = 6.46, id 66). Q4 FY26: TPU units (UBS, Morgan Stanley, Epoch: src 121, 122, 123; src 121 cleared by a none-newer search 2026-11-18) x revenue per unit; FY2027/FY2028: customer GW x $/GW (inputs_detail rows 'AI revenue per GW', 'FY2027 AI revenue', 'FY2028 * GW realised', source ids 37, 38, 47, 48). Kuo cut: analyst survey (Ming-Chi Kuo's X post of 2026-11-20, robots-blocked, cited through the dated relays src 171, src 172, src 173, src 183; analyst Kuo's 2026-11-16 unit survey src 181, src 182); designers per CEO Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call (src 38); networking supply agreement and LTA src 174; FY28-29 v9 design split reconciled 2026-11-23 on src 178, src 188 (TrendForce), src 189, src 190, src 181, src 182 (analyst Kuo's 11-16 survey) and src 191 (Kuo's June Humufish units, cross-check only), src 174 (LTA, networking) (MediaTek CEO src 175 names no customer; JPMorgan's 2026-06-17 note via KuCoin, src 144, past the 90-day sell-side window, background only).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 21,496 built from units x revenue per unit (rebuild 2026-11-09, networking rebuilt 2026-11-17; was 22,177 = guide x the median beat). Units (estimate): Broadcom TPUs CY2026 ~3.215M = the set's average of UBS analysts' 3.68M Broadcom TPUs for 2026 [src 121] and Morgan Stanley's 3.2M TPUs in 2026 [src 122] less MediaTek's 0.45M (UBS analysts) [src 121] (reading Morgan Stanley's figure as the all-designer total is the set's inference): (3.68 + 2.75) / 2 = 3.215M. Jan-Jul ~1.429M from Epoch (Q3 FY26 ~800k, up ~65% q/q, so Q2 ~485k; Q1 ~433k at the middle of the +2% to +22% quarterly range, one third of it in January = 144k [src 123]); the remaining 1.786M over Aug-Dec, rising evenly from a ~300k July month, gives Aug-Oct ~1.014M (319k + 338k + 357k). XPU revenue per unit $15.56k (estimate) = Q3 FY26 $15.24k (XPU revenue 16,700 x 0.73 = 12,191 / ~800k units) + $0.32k more HBM as TPU 8i (288 GB vs Ironwood's ~192 GB [src 126]) ramps to a quarter of units: 96 GB x ~$12.2/GB HBM3e [src 127] x 0.25 x 1.1 (memory resold at ~10%, judgment). Q3 FY26 call: Broadcom to 'ramp up high-volume shipments of the TPU version 8i to Google' and 'accelerate shipments of Ironwood to Anthropic' (ids 37, 38). XPU 1,014k x $15.56k = 15,778. AI networking from the compute it connects (rebuild 2026-11-17, carry-forward fix; was Q3 FY26's filed ratio to all XPU revenue, 5,836): Q3 FY26 networking 4,509 = 16,700 x (1 - 0.73) (Q3 FY26 call: XPUs 'represented 73% of AI revenue', ids 37, 38) = 0.445 x the non-HBM part of XPU revenue 12,191 x (1 - 16.9%); Q4 HBM is 18.6% of XPU revenue as TPU 8i ramps. Both HBM shares are the set's estimates (xpu_margin row): capacities from Tom's Hardware (src 126), the HBM3e price from Silicon Analysts (src 127), the division the set's; neither page gives an HBM share, networking or XPU revenue, so networking = 0.445 x 15,778 x 0.814 = 5,718 (switch, scale-up and optics ports scale with compute, not memory GB; Q3 FY26 call: Tomahawk Ultra 'deployed starting actually this quarter', networking 'expected to grow just as fast as XPUs', ids 37, 38). Total 21,496; XPU share 0.734. Range 17.65B (Morgan Stanley units only) to 25.6B (UBS units only), both sized in judgment_alternatives; the $21.7B company guide is the cross-check (-0.9%). FY27 118,150 from customer GW (rebuild 2026-11-09; was 10 GW x $11.5B, a price chosen to match the $115B outlook): Anthropic 5.0 GW ('another 5 gigawatts of TPU version 8i in 2027'), OpenAI 1.3 GW ('planned deployment of 1.3 gigawatts in 2027'), Meta 1.0 GW ('line of sight to deploy 3 gigawatts through 28', about a third a year over 2026-2028) (ids 37, 38) x $11.5B per GW (Rasgon midpoint, owner card 2026-11-10) = 83,950; plus Google's own TPUs: $25B a year (the set's middle of $20-30B, its reading of 'multi-tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually', id 38; $30B is sized as an alternative) with networking at the 0.73 XPU share = 25,000 / 0.73 = 34,247, booked as 34,200. Total 118,150. Mizuho (id 48) puts Broadcom's Anthropic AI revenue at $21B for 2026 and $42B for 2027 and, separately, the Anthropic deal at ~3.5 GW from 2027; it gives no per-GW price, so any per-GW figure from it is the set's division ($12.0B on 3.5 GW, $8.4B on the 5 GW Tan now cites, ~$21B on 2026's 1 GW). drivers.label: Custom XPU share of AI semiconductor revenue (rest = AI networking)
drivers.source: Calls: Q1 FY26 'AI networking ... represented one third of total AI revenue' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/03/04/broadcom-avgo-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript); Q2 FY26 'Networking represented almost 40% of our Q2 AI revenue' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/03/broadcom-avgo-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/); Q3 FY26 XPUs 'represented 73% of AI revenue' (ids 37, 38). Outlook: Q2 FY26 call, networking share 'closer to around 30%' and 40% 'probably as high as' it goes; Q3 FY26 call, networking 'expected to grow just as fast as XPUs over the next few years'; Q4 FY26 'both XPUs and AI networking revenue to triple year on year'. (Q1 FY26 id 87; Q2 FY26 id 88) Q4 FY25 call (id 77): of the $73B AI backlog 'maybe $20 billion of it is everything else. The rest, is XPUs.'
drivers.derivation: Actuals FY26: 0.667 / 0.61 / 0.73 (cited). FY25 quarters 0.65: not read from the FY25 calls (base year only; feeds no forecast and no filed-quarter EBIT). Q4 FY26 0.734 (rebuild 2026-11-17; was 0.73 at Q3 FY26's filed ratio, and 0.663 from the Q4 'both triple' outlook before 2026-11-09): XPU 15,778 / AI 21,496, networking tied to non-HBM XPU content as for FY27-29 below. FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix; the 0.73 for every quarter repeated the last filed split): networking is built from the compute it connects, XPU revenue from compute plus the HBM Broadcom resells inside it. Q3 FY26: networking 4,509 (16,700 x 0.27) = 0.370 x XPU revenue 12,191 (16,700 x 0.73; the call's 'represented 73% of AI revenue', ids 37, 38), and HBM was ~16.9% of XPU revenue (the set's estimate in the xpu_margin build: Ironwood's ~192 GB from Tom's Hardware, src 126, x the HBM3e price ~$12.2/GB from Silicon Analysts, src 127, x 1.1, over the set's $15.24k XPU revenue per unit; neither page gives an HBM share), so networking = 0.445 x the non-HBM part of XPU revenue (0.370 / 0.831). Switch, scale-up and optics ports scale with compute dies and cluster size, not with memory GB, and the Q3 FY26 call ties the networking outlook to XPU deployments ('expected to grow just as fast as XPUs over the next few years'; Tomahawk 6 and Tomahawk Ultra 'deployed in pretty much all of the AI hyperscalers that are building XPUs with us', ids 37, 38), while the CFO names 'the increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content' (id 38). HBM share of XPU revenue by year from the set's own xpu_margin build (until the 2026-11-23 owner picks below): FY27 23.4% (TPU 8i, 288 GB, every XPU), FY28 31.5% (TPU revenue share 0.675, half of it on TPU v9 at 47.5% HBM per owner card 2026-11-16 'v9 HBM4, half of FY28', rest 23.4%), FY29 39.5% (TPU 0.669 all v9, non-TPU 23.4%). XPU share = 1 / (1 + 0.445 x (1 - HBM share)): FY27 0.7457, FY28 0.7664, FY29 0.7879, the same each quarter of a year (the HBM shares are yearly, as in xpu_margin). Reading 'grow just as fast' as revenue would keep the share at Q3 FY26's 0.73; that, the Q2 FY26 call's networking 'closer to around 30%' (0.70, id 88) and the HBM step on TPUs only are sized as alternatives. Moderately conservative: a higher XPU share lowers the AI margin (networking ~72% vs XPUs 46-56%). Not changed here: the FY27 Google TPU line in ai_rev, grossed up for networking at 0.73 (25,000 / 0.73), which at the rebuilt 0.7457 would be 25,000 / 0.7457; sized as an ai_rev alternative. | SemiAnalysis cut: owner pick 2026-11-17 (Owner card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLHb22faGDqKhees5ZNgh1HH) 'Volume net of moratorium') books it as volume on ai_rev, so this driver stays on its 11-16 path. | Kuo cut 2026-11-20: the cut removes XPU revenue only (networking held: the 8-K's networking supply agreement for Google's next-generation AI racks through up to 2031, src 174, supports the networking hold only; reading the cut as XPU-only is the set's reading of the analyst's survey), so each forecast quarter's share = (pre-cut XPU - cut) / (pre-cut AI - cut): FY27 0.7160, FY28 0.7319, FY29 0.7571 (v9 reconciliation 2026-11-23: Google's own Broadcom TPU line gone from January 2028; the half-of-v9 middle 0.7410 / 0.7735; first pass 0.7424 / 0.7684; before the cut 0.7457 / 0.7664 / 0.7879). | Owner picks 2026-11-23 (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLJpix3hq1zVuAhfJTrJzQoH '8i margin level 55.9%'): with no v9 HBM4 step, the xpu_margin build gives every XPU the 8i HBM share 23.4% in FY28-29 as in FY27, so the pre-cut share is 0.7457 in every FY27-29 quarter (1 / (1 + 0.445 x 0.766)); each quarter keeps its Kuo cut as a share of its AI revenue (networking held): FY28 quarters 0.6913 / 0.7025 / 0.7112 / 0.7187, FY29 0.6911 / 0.7029 / 0.7115 / 0.7190; FY28 0.7081, FY29 0.7088 (were 0.7319 / 0.7571 on the v9 step's 31.5% / 39.5% HBM shares). Less HBM in the same $11.5B per GW leaves more of it to networking.
drivers.why: Mix lever: networking earns ~72% and XPUs ~52-59%, so each point of share moves the AI margin by ~0.2pt.
drivers.variant: Upside mix: 0.73 kept (Q3 FY26 split, 'grow just as fast as XPUs' read as revenue, ids 37, 38) or 0.70 (Q2 FY26 call: networking 'closer to around 30%', id 88); downside: higher still if rack-level systems are booked in the XPU line (no source shows this yet).

Q3: 192 GB x $12.2 x 1.1 = $2.58k of $15.24k per unit = 16.9%; Q4: +$0.32k = $2.90k of $15.56k = 18.6%. Memory resold at ~10% margin (judgment) vs ~69.5% on the rest, the split that gives Q3's filed-derived margin: (59.45% - 16.9% x 10%) / 83.1% = 69.5%; step 1.7pt x (69.5% - 10%) = -1.0pt; CFO: 'the increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content ... is diluting our consolidated gross margin', ids 37, 38), plus ~0.3pt as semiconductor opex ($1.2B in Q3, 'OpEx representing 6% of segment revenue') spreads over more revenue. FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-16 (thread 'Source AVGO TPU margin and FY29 AI revenue'; was 58.75% held, owner card 2026-11-09 'Hold both flat' was on the UBS rack-margin question; gate 2026-11-16 failed the hold as unsupported): 55.90% for every XPU. TPUs: the Q3 FY26 call transcript (id 38, re-opened 2026-11-18) says 'Broadcom is now shipping the TPU version 8i ahead of the MediaTek version v8t', 'ramp up high-volume shipments of the TPU version 8i to Google' and 'We expect Anthropic to deploy another 5 gigawatts of TPU version 8i in 2027', so Broadcom's 2027 TPU units are 8i. Memory per chip (288 GB) is from Tom's Hardware (src 126; the page has no margin or HBM-share figure; Tom's Hardware and other press name MediaTek for 8i and Broadcom for 8t; CEO Hock Tan's 'Broadcom is now shipping the TPU version 8i ahead of the MediaTek version v8t' (src 38) and Kuo's 2026-11-20 survey (Broadcom-designed 8i, MediaTek-designed 8t) contradict them, so that reading is kept only as a sized alternative). The set's formula: HBM 288 GB x $12.2/GB (src 127, HBM3E 2026 per-stack blend) x 1.1 = $3.87k of $16.53k per unit = 23.4% of revenue; 76.6% x 69.5% + 23.4% x 10% + 0.3pt opex leverage = 55.90%. Non-TPU XPUs (OpenAI Jalapeno, Meta MTIA): no source gives their HBM content (searched 2026-11-16); the CFO's 'increasing mix of XPUs with their increasing memory content ... diluting our consolidated gross margin' (Q3 FY26, id 38) is about XPUs generally, so they take the same HBM share (the conservative reading; the 58.75% hold is sized as an alternative). FY28-FY29 carried, from 2026-11-16 until the owner's 2026-11-23 pick below superseded it, the TPU v9 HBM step (owner card 2026-11-16 12:47Z 'v9 HBM4, half of FY28'): JPMorgan's 2026-06-17 note (Harlan Sur, as relayed by KuCoin 2026-06-29, src 144; past the 90-day sell-side window, so the timing now rests on TrendForce 2026-10-19, src 178, shipments 1Q28, and the analyst's 2026-11-16 survey, src 181) has Broadcom's 2nm program ramping in volume in 2028, and the KuCoin article itself (not JPMorgan) gives v9 four compute dies and 16 HBM stacks; build = 16 x 36 GB HBM4 12-hi stacks = 576 GB x $36.11/GB (Silicon Analysts, CY2027 supply expected, src 127) x 1.1 = $22.88k per chip on non-HBM value 2x 8i's $12.66k (four compute dies; the set's estimate) -> HBM 47.5% of TPU revenue, TPU margin 41.6%; v9 on half of FY28 TPU revenue (ramp year) and all of FY29, TPU revenue shares from the ai_rev rows (FY28 0.675, FY29 0.669), non-TPU and 8i units at 55.90% -> FY28 51.06%, FY29 46.30%. Caveat: revenue per GW stays $11.5B, so HBM4 cost passed through is not added to revenue. CEO Hock Tan cross-check: 'sustain operating margin even as mix of products dilutes the gross margin' (consolidated, id 38). | SemiAnalysis cut: owner pick 2026-11-17 (Owner card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET (cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLHb22faGDqKhees5ZNgh1HH) 'Volume net of moratorium') books it as volume on ai_rev, so this driver stays on its 11-16 path. | v9 reconciliation 2026-11-23 (owner pick stands, consequence sized, not applied): TrendForce 2026-10-22 (src 188) lists 'Broadcom-designed WhaleFish, and MediaTek-designed HumuFish and TriggerFish' with a 'Google-designed Compute Die A'; analyst Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International Securities; 2026-11-16 survey via ChainCatcher src 189 and China Times src 190) has MediaTek the 'sole design supplier for v9 (Humufish and Triggerfish)' and 'the main shipments until 2029 will still be from the v8 series', with v8 orders from OpenAI and Anthropic; his 2026-11-20 post puts WhaleFish with the 8i Max being cut (src 171, src 173). So Broadcom ships no Humufish: its FY28-29 TPUs are the 8i for Anthropic (v8 series) plus what is left of WhaleFish / 8i Max (two 8i dies, 384 GB HBM3e, src 145), none of them a 576 GB HBM4 part. The owner's v9 step therefore has no Broadcom v9 HBM4 revenue to apply to; on that reading FY28-29 sit at the full-8i 55.90% (sized alternative 'TPU v9 not modeled'). The booked 51.06% / 46.30% stayed on the owner card 2026-11-16 until Kilian re-decided on 2026-11-23 (below); the step carried mechanically onto the reconciled TPU share (Google's own TPU line gone, TPU 0.608 / 0.602 of XPU revenue instead of 0.675 / 0.669) would be 51.54% / 47.26%, also sized. | Owner picks 2026-11-23 (Kilian's card 2026-11-23 15:53:48Z, cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLJpix3hq1zVuAhfJTrJzQoH: 'Re-decide the v9 memory step on Broadcom's chip margin now that Broadcom builds no Humufish?' -> '8i margin level 55.9%'; supersedes the 2026-11-16 12:47Z pick 'v9 HBM4, half of FY28'): FY28-29 at the full-8i 55.90% (its alternative 'TPU v9 not modeled', patch xpu_margin quarters 12-19 = 0.559). On the v9 reconciliation Broadcom's FY28-29 TPUs are Anthropic's 8i and what is left of WhaleFish / 8i Max on HBM3e (src 188, src 189, src 190, src 171, src 173, src 145), so the set's formula gives every XPU the 8i memory share as in FY27: 288 GB x $12.2/GB x 1.1 = $3.87k of $16.53k = 23.4%; 76.6% x 69.5% + 23.4% x 10% + 0.3pt opex leverage = 55.90%. The 2026-11-16 v9 HBM4 step (51.06% / 46.30%) is kept as a sized alternative; xpu_share FY28-29 follows on the same 23.4% HBM share (its row).

drivers.label: Infrastructure software revenue (VMware and mainframe/enterprise software)
drivers.source: Actuals = Infrastructure software segment revenue (id 68). Q4 FY26: Q3 FY26 call (ids 37, 38): 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (declared guide use, guidance_check 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026); 'we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year'. Gartner via The Register (https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/); CloudBolt via Petri (https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 8,700: the company figure, 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (Q3 FY26 call, ids 37, 38), used as a declared last resort (guidance_check row 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026, guide_use): Broadcom gives no VMware renewal calendar, and recognized software revenue does not track the one disclosed driver, ARR (Q3 FY26 revenue 8,752 was +29% y/y against ARR +15%), so no driver build sets one quarter. Its FY26 record: Q1 FY26 guide ~$6.8B vs 6,796 (-0.06%), Q2 FY26 guide ~$7.2B vs 7,178 (-0.3%), Q3 FY26 guide ~$8.9B vs 8,752 (-1.7%); the guide x the Q2-Q3 FY26 average miss (8,614) is sized as an alternative. Was 8,750 (gate 2026-11-17: the guide booked without a declaration). FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix): revenue follows VMware's recurring base, which is the installed workloads times the price per workload. (1) Today: ARR +15% y/y at Q3 FY26 ('we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year', id 38; +17% at Q2 FY26, id 88) and management expected the faster VMware growth 'to continue' (Q2 FY26 call, June 2026, id 88). That growth is the first Broadcom-era repricing onto VCF: in CloudBolt's January 2026 survey 14% of customers saw increases above 100%, 12% 50-99%, 33% 24-49% and 31% below 25% (via Petri, https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/). (2) Workloads: Gartner expects 'More than a third of workloads currently running under VMware will run on another platform by 2028' (The Register, 2025-09-11, https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/): 35% lost over Sep 2025-Dec 2028 = -12.4% a year; CloudBolt: '86% of organizations report actively reducing their VMware footprint'. (3) Once the first repricing has passed through the base, growth = renewal share x renewal uplift less attrition: a third of the base renews each year (three-year VCF subscriptions; estimate) at +24%, the bottom of the survey's median bucket (24-49%) as a second-cycle uplift (judgment, moderately conservative), so (1 + 0.24 / 3) x (1 - 12.4%) - 1 = -5.4% a year. Path: ARR growth fades from +15% (Q3 FY26) to -5.4% by Q4 FY27 in even steps (+9.9%, +4.8%, -0.3%, -5.4% annualised in Q1-Q4 FY27; 'multiple quarters' from June 2026), then -5.4% a year in FY28; each quarter = the one before x (1 + annual rate)^(1/4). FY29 (Nov 2028-Oct 2029) runs past Gartner's 'by 2028' window, so no source covers it: the -5.4% a year there is judgment (moderately conservative: attrition is assumed to go on at Gartner's pace for one more year); attrition ending (+8% a year, renewal uplift only) and a flat FY29 are sized as alternatives. FY27 35,807.6, FY28 34,317.2, FY29 32,461.4. Alternatives sized: flat at 8,700 ('approximately $8.7 billion'), ARR +15% a year, no second-cycle uplift, uplift at the median bucket's middle (36%), Q4 at the guide x the median miss, FY29 attrition ending. Margin: constant sw_margin (94% gross margin less a judgment $919M opex a quarter).
drivers.why: ~25% of FY26 revenue at ~84% margin; the stable earnings floor.

drivers.label: Customer-financing exposure backed by Broadcom (probability-weighted, utilised)
drivers.source: 10-Q 2026-08-02 R17/R54: Backstop max ~$29B, $42B convertible-note facility (ids 29, 31); 8-K Item 2.03 2026-10-27: SPV Backstop max ~$43B (id 67); OpenAI >$50B package (WSJ, id 45); XPV aims '>20 gigawatts ... by the end of 2028' (ids 37, 38).
drivers.derivation: Each deal at its maximum x 70% average utilisation x probability Broadcom carries it: 10-Q Backstop 29,000 x 0.7 = 20,300 and Anthropic senior notes 42,000 x 0.7 = 29,400 (Q3 FY26, 49,700); Oct 27 SPV Backstop 43,000 x 0.7 = 30,100 (Q4 FY26, 79,800); OpenAI 35,000 x p 0.6 x 0.7 = 14,700 (from Q2 FY27, 94,500); future XPV backstops 32,000 x p 0.5 x 0.7 = 11,200 (from Q2 FY28, 105,700). The loss uses the FY28 year-end stock (every deal expected by 2028). FY2029 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix; was the FY28 stock 105,700 in every quarter): the backstops fall as the leases are paid. The Oct 27 8-K says the Backstop maximum is reached on deployment and the liability is 'rising with deliveries and falling with lease payments' (id 67); the 10-Q Backstop covers 5-year leases (ids 29, 31). Each deal's FY28 stock is run forward by its remaining rent: cohorts amortise straight-line over 5 years from lease start, so remaining(t) = sum of each cohort's 1 - (t - start) / 5, and FY29 = FY28 stock x remaining(t) / remaining(FY28 end). Lease starts (estimate): 10-Q Backstop evenly over Q1-Q2 FY27 (the $35B tranche closed June 2026 for Anthropic's 1 GW; Reuters on the prospectus: expanded TPU access 'beginning in 2027', src 141); Oct 27 SPV over FY27 on the FY24-26 quarter shape (Anthropic's 5 GW of TPU 8i in 2027, id 38); OpenAI package over Q2 FY27-Q4 FY28 by the set's GW (1.3 FY27, 3.5 FY28); future XPV over Q2-Q4 FY28 (XPV 'by the end of 2028', ids 37, 38). Anthropic notes 29,400: no repayment in FY29, as the 10-Q gives no maturity or amortisation for the notes and they fund the lease rent (id 29). No new Broadcom-backed deal in FY29: no source names one (the OpenAI 10 GW deal runs to end-2029, src 142, but the WSJ package, id 45, is the only financing reported; financing for FY29's 3.64 GW at the FY27-28 ratio is sized as an alternative). Q4 FY29 by deal: 10-Q Backstop 14087, SPV 21694, OpenAI 11310, XPV 8805, notes 29,400. FY29 quarters 100,599 / 95,498 / 90,397 / 85,296. Caveat: the liability is the covered share of rent owed less the racks' resale value, so it falls with rent only if rack value falls in step (judgment). Value-neutral: the expected-loss adjustment reads the FY28 stock (cf_exposure_y3).
drivers.why: Replaces the fixed -4,568 adjustment: loss = exposure x loss rate.

drivers.label: Optics share of AI networking revenue (optical DSPs + EML/CW/VCSEL lasers + CPO)
drivers.source: Not disclosed by Broadcom. Company: CEO Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call: 'leader in leading-edge optical DSPs', 'leader in EMLs, VCSELs, and CW lasers' with 'a fairly substantial share'; Charlie Kawwas (President, Semiconductor Solutions Group): laser/InP fabs 'more than tripling' y/y (id 76); CEO Hock Tan, Q4 FY25 call: lasers 'relatively lesser dollars' than XPUs, ~$20B of the $73B AI backlog is switches + DSPs + lasers (id 77). Market: AI optical transceivers ~$16.5B in 2025 (TrendForce via Aetrix, id 78); LightCounting 2026-10-08: Ethernet optical transceiver sales +120% in 2026, +76% in 2027 (src 162); TrendForce 2026-11-02: pluggable transceivers $84.1B in 2027, +76% (src 161); DSP 20-40% of an 800G BOM (id 79); Marvell 60-65% of 'one key type' of the signal-processing chips it sells to optical module makers (Stifel via TheStreet, id 80; the page does not name the type: reading it as optical DSPs, the Broadcom/Marvell duopoly of id 81, is the set's inference), a Broadcom/Marvell duopoly (id 81); 1.6T chipsets >$2B in 2026 (LightCounting, id 84); Lumentum 50-60% of EMLs (id 83), Lumentum+Broadcom+Mitsubishi ~72% of EMLs, Broadcom a CW-DFB leader (TrendForce, id 78); Lumentum Components revenue $443.7M / $533.3M / $649.4M / $754.2M in its quarters ended Dec 2025 - Sep 2026 (Lumentum 8-Ks, src 164, src 163).
drivers.derivation: Rebuilt 2026-11-18 (carry trace: Q4 FY26 0.1135 was the base round's value while the text quoting it had moved to the rebuilt networking). FY26 Broadcom optics ~$2.49B = optical DSPs ~$1.91B + lasers ~$0.58B + CPO ~0 (pre-volume). DSPs: 2026 AI optical transceiver market $36.3B = 2025 $16.5B (TrendForce, id 78) x 2.2 (LightCounting's +120% for 2026, src 162); x 0.70 BOM/price (judgment: module makers' ~30% gross margin) x 0.25 (low-middle of 20-40%, id 79) = DSP market ~$6.35B; x Broadcom ~30% (100% - Marvell 62.5% (Stifel's unnamed chip type read as optical DSPs, id 80) - others ~7.5%) = $1.91B. TrendForce's newer 2026-11-02 release implies ~$47.8B for 2026 (2027 $84.1B / 1.76, src 161); the lower LightCounting reading is booked under the moderately conservative base case and the TrendForce reading is sized as an alternative. Was $26B (TrendForce April, id 78), overtaken by both. Lasers: Lumentum Components over the four quarters that match Broadcom's FY26 (Dec 2025 - Sep 2026) = 443.7 + 533.3 + 649.4 + 754.2 = $2,380.6M (src 164, src 163; was the single Jun-2026 quarter x 4); x 75% datacom lasers (judgment: the rest is telecom and pump lasers, which led its Sep quarter) = $1,785M; / ~55% Lumentum share (id 83) = datacom laser market ~$3.25B; x Broadcom ~18% blended (EML ~8.5% [TrendForce via Aetrix: Lumentum + Broadcom + Mitsubishi ~72% of EML, id 78, less Lumentum ~55%, id 83, split with Mitsubishi]; CW ~25% and VCSEL ~30% are the set's judgment, low confidence: no source gives Broadcom's CW or VCSEL share, Aetrix/TrendForce only lists Broadcom among the CW-DFB leaders whose top four hold ~74% of capacity, id 78, and the CEO claims 'a fairly substantial share', id 76) = $0.58B (CW and VCSEL at the EML ~8.5% instead: lasers $0.28B, optics share 12.68%, sized as an optics_share alternative). FY26 AI networking from the quarter xpu_shares on the booked Q4 FY26: 8,400 x (1 - 0.6667) + 10,800 x (1 - 0.61) + 16,700 x (1 - 0.73) + 21,496 x (1 - 0.734) = 2,799.7 + 4,212.0 + 4,509.0 + 5,717.9 = 17,238.7. Share = 2,490.1 / 17,238.7 = 14.44%, booked for every FY26 quarter including Q4 (no source gives optics by quarter). Value-neutral by itself: optics stays at the 72% networking margin (no cited split); it sizes the Marvell-Lumentum effect. FY27-FY29 held at the FY26 level (owner card 2026-11-09 'Hold both flat'): no source sizes a rising share; LightCounting expects linear-drive optics to cut DSP sales (id 84) and TrendForce has CPO moving value from pluggables into switches (src 161), against lasers 'far surpassing supply' (id 76). Was 11.35% (2026-11-17, $26B transceivers and one Lumentum quarter x 4), 10.4% before.
drivers.why: Sizes the exposure to the combined Marvell-Lumentum: FY28 optics ~$6.2B (Q4 FY28 run-rate ~$7.9B on the booked AI revenue).
drivers.variant: TrendForce's 2026-11-02 reading (2026 transceivers ~$47.8B, src 161): 17.95% of networking, the deal effect x1.24.

drivers.source: Deal: 4.5 MRVL per LITE, close expected 1H CY2028, 'pre-validated optical solutions' (lasers, transceivers, OCS, InP) (id 75); Broadcom today the only full optical path to a hyperscaler (id 82); Lumentum NPO/CPO win backed by >$5B commitments (id 85). drivers.label: AI/data-center revenue lost to US data-center moratoria (expected share)
drivers.source: Scenario weights and no redirect: owner decision card 2026-11-05 ('Book it with spread at 30%'; thread 'Size moratorium risk for AVGO and NVDA'); proposal driver_models/AVGO/moratorium_proposal_avgo_nvda.md; sources [src 89, 90, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 109, 110, 111, 112, 116, 117].
drivers.derivation: Expected share of Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue (ai_rev: XPUs and AI networking) lost to US data-center moratoria. Haircut = US deployment share x affected-state share x early-stage share x share of the window delayed; no redirect (owner decision card 2026-11-05). US share 0.693 = NVIDIA FY2026 revenue billed in the United States $149,617M / $215,938M [src 93] (NVIDIA's 10-K revenue by region, billing location, borrowed for AVGO, which discloses no deployment split: flagged). State shares, capacity basis for every state (owner 2026-11-05: 'everything should be on a capacity basis'): dcmap.us pipeline GW (under construction + planned, the stock the early-stage haircut acts on; operating capacity excluded), 'Data updated Oct 2026', read 2026-11-05 [src 116]; US pipeline 345.9 GW = 69.6 under construction + 276.3 planned [src 116, 117]. Texas 19.5 + 73.6 = 93.1 GW = 0.2692. PJM states VA 8.3+23.3 = 31.6, PA 8.1+15 = 23.1, OH 3.8+13.8 = 17.6, IL 1.9+8.7 = 10.6, NJ 0.340+0.295 = 0.635, MD 0.444+1.1 = 1.544, half of IN (4.1+4.6)/2 = 4.35: 89.429 GW = 0.2585 (Texas + PJM 0.5277). Georgia 1.2+18.6 = 19.8 GW = 0.0572, spread scenario only (weight 0.30, like PJM; owner card 2026-11-05 'Georgia in spread scenario'): ABC News projected Bottoms to win (2026-11-03 [src 109]) and said 'We need to pause' [src 110]; Bloomberg: called for a moratorium on new construction [src 107]; no scope or duration given. New York 0.382+5.7 = 6.082 GW = 0.0176. Caveat (flagged): dcmap's figures are 'reported or announced' and rounded, and a project's figure may be IT load, utility service or whole-campus power. Cross-checks: SemiAnalysis via Bloomberg: Texas 'nearly 30%' of US capacity coming online in 2028 [src 107]; BNEF ~20% of the US pipeline [src 90]; UBS via Finimize (2026-11-04): 'about 30% of expected 2028 capacity additions at risk' [src 111], not booked separately. Replaces this morning's mixed basis (Texas 0.29 capacity, others Cleanview building counts). Early stage 0.70 (BNEF via Utility Dive: 'more than 70%' of ~50 GW of Texas projects early stage [src 90]). Texas measures: ERCOT 'has paused the energization of new Large Load data centers' not yet connected 'until the completion of the verification and audit and community impact review', with the verification and community-impact reports to be filed with the PUCT by 2026-12-10 and a 'TBD impact' on the Batch Zero timeline [src 97, 96], after the Governor's directive to the PUCT and ERCOT to audit all data centers in the interconnection process before any more advance [src 98]; TCEQ data-center permits paused 'until ERCOT completes its review' (letter 2026-09-21) [src 99]. None of these sets a duration. Timing (gate 2026-11-05, same evidence and timing as the NVDA round): no Texas source sets an end date; the pause ends with the 2026-12-10 reports or, in the Texas-pause scenario, when the Legislature acts: Hinojosa called for a moratorium 'until a legislative session that puts Texans first' / until the legislature 'can adopt statewide regulations' [src 101, 102]; the 90th regular session runs 2027-01-12 to 2027-05-31 [src 103, 104]. So a 10-month pause, 2026-08-03 to 2027-05-31 (estimate, low confidence). An early-stage site takes about 12 months from construction start to operation at the fast end (Stargate Abilene buildings 1-2 operational 12 months after construction began [src 106]; Epoch AI: 1 to 3.6 years to 1 GW [src 105]), so the pause first removes installed accelerators about 2027-08 and pushes those projects out by its length: calendar Aug 2027-May 2028, window share 1.0 (estimate). The PJM spread is assumed on the same timing (estimate: no PJM state has a pause in force). Non-AI margin = non-AI gross margin less non-AI operating expenses over non-AI revenue. Gross margin ~70%: Q4 FY23 segment gross margin ~70% when non-AI was ~$5.8B of $7.3B (CFO, src 129); non-AI prices have been held (no cut named on any call since). Operating expenses ~$0.62B a quarter: the segment's $822M in Q4 FY23 ('stable year-on-year') less ~25% for the AI R&D already in it (AI ~20% of Q4 FY23 segment revenue, judgment); every increase since (to $1.1B in Q4 FY25 and $1.2B in Q3 FY26) is named as AI R&D ('increased investment in R&D for leading-edge AI semiconductors', src 130; Q3 FY26 'reflected investments in R&D', ids 37, 38). On Q3 FY26 non-AI revenue of $4.14B that is 15.0% of revenue: 70% - 15% = 55%. Forward (rebuilt 2026-11-17, carry-forward fix; was 55% every quarter): the same formula each quarter, 70% less $0.62B over that quarter's non-AI revenue (constant non_ai_rev), so the margin moves with revenue: Q4 FY26 55.6%, FY27-FY29 55.0%-57.2% (the cost base stays at $0.62B because every opex increase since FY23 is named as AI R&D, src 130). Range 54-56% for non-AI opex $0.58-0.66B; ~59% if Broadcom cut non-AI R&D in line with the ~30% fall in non-AI revenue since FY23 (no filing says so). inputs_detail.value: Infrastructure software revenue (VMware and mainframe/enterprise software): FY26 31,426.0 -> FY27 35,807.6 / FY28 34,317.2 / FY29 32,461.4 (estimate; Q4 FY26 at the ~$8.7B company figure as a declared guide use; ARR growth fading to -5.4% a year: Gartner workload attrition vs renewal repricing, FY29 judgment; quarterly, sum)
inputs_detail.source: Actuals = Infrastructure software segment revenue (id 68). Q4 FY26: Q3 FY26 call (ids 37, 38): 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (declared guide use, guidance_check 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026); 'we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year'. Gartner via The Register (https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/); CloudBolt via Petri (https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/).
inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 FY26 8,700: the company figure, 'We expect Q4 infrastructure software revenue of approximately $8.7 billion' (Q3 FY26 call, ids 37, 38), used as a declared last resort (guidance_check row 'infrastructure software revenue' Q4 FY2026, guide_use): Broadcom gives no VMware renewal calendar, and recognized software revenue does not track the one disclosed driver, ARR (Q3 FY26 revenue 8,752 was +29% y/y against ARR +15%), so no driver build sets one quarter. Its FY26 record: Q1 FY26 guide ~$6.8B vs 6,796 (-0.06%), Q2 FY26 guide ~$7.2B vs 7,178 (-0.3%), Q3 FY26 guide ~$8.9B vs 8,752 (-1.7%); the guide x the Q2-Q3 FY26 average miss (8,614) is sized as an alternative. Was 8,750 (gate 2026-11-17: the guide booked without a declaration). FY27-FY29 rebuilt 2026-11-17 (carry-forward fix): revenue follows VMware's recurring base, which is the installed workloads times the price per workload. (1) Today: ARR +15% y/y at Q3 FY26 ('we sustained ARR growth of 15% year-on-year', id 38; +17% at Q2 FY26, id 88) and management expected the faster VMware growth 'to continue' (Q2 FY26 call, June 2026, id 88). That growth is the first Broadcom-era repricing onto VCF: in CloudBolt's January 2026 survey 14% of customers saw increases above 100%, 12% 50-99%, 33% 24-49% and 31% below 25% (via Petri, https://petri.com/vmware-pricing-fears-enterprise-virtualization-shift/). (2) Workloads: Gartner expects 'More than a third of workloads currently running under VMware will run on another platform by 2028' (The Register, 2025-09-11, https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/11/gartner_vmware_migration_advice/): 35% lost over Sep 2025-Dec 2028 = -12.4% a year; CloudBolt: '86% of organizations report actively reducing their VMware footprint'. (3) Once the first repricing has passed through the base, growth = renewal share x renewal uplift less attrition: a third of the base renews each year (three-year VCF subscriptions; estimate) at +24%, the bottom of the survey's median bucket (24-49%) as a second-cycle uplift (judgment, moderately conservative), so (1 + 0.24 / 3) x (1 - 12.4%) - 1 = -5.4% a year. Path: ARR growth fades from +15% (Q3 FY26) to -5.4% by Q4 FY27 in even steps (+9.9%, +4.8%, -0.3%, -5.4% annualised in Q1-Q4 FY27; 'multiple quarters' from June 2026), then -5.4% a year in FY28; each quarter = the one before x (1 + annual rate)^(1/4). FY29 (Nov 2028-Oct 2029) runs past Gartner's 'by 2028' window, so no source covers it: the -5.4% a year there is judgment (moderately conservative: attrition is assumed to go on at Gartner's pace for one more year); attrition ending (+8% a year, renewal uplift only) and a flat FY29 are sized as alternatives. FY27 35,807.6, FY28 34,317.2, FY29 32,461.4. Alternatives sized: flat at 8,700 ('approximately $8.7 billion'), ARR +15% a year, no second-cycle uplift, uplift at the median bucket's middle (36%), Q4 at the guide x the median miss, FY29 attrition ending. Margin: constant sw_margin (94% gross margin less a judgment $919M opex a quarter).

inputs_detail.derivation: Kuo cut (update 2026-11-20, built ground-up; FY28-29 and the unit check rebuilt at the 2026-11-23 gate fix): analyst Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International Securities; his X post of 2026-11-20 is robots-blocked, so it is cited through the dated relays that quote it: Stock Analysis 2026-11-20, src 171, TheStreet 2026-11-22, src 172, NineZenith 2026-11-22, src 173, and Seeking Alpha 2026-11-20, src 183) says his 'latest industry survey indicates Google has cut 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by ~1M units (mostly the higher-priced 8i Max / Whalefish). The cut amounts to roughly 20% of 2027 TPU 8i series shipments', and that Google 'plans to increase 2027 shipments of the MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series, though details aren't final yet'. It is an analyst's survey, not a company statement (rule 25); neither Google nor Broadcom had commented (src 171, src 172). Designers: Broadcom designs the 8i and MediaTek the 8t. CEO Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call (src 38): 'Broadcom is now shipping the TPU version 8i ahead of the MediaTek version v8t, which, in fact, was initiated earlier' and 'We expect Anthropic to deploy another 5 gigawatts of TPU version 8i in 2027'; the analyst's split agrees. Tom's Hardware (src 126) pairs them the other way round ('MediaTek understood to be handling the design of the TPU 8i'); the CEO contradicts it, so that reading is dropped. Size: Broadcom's 2027 8i XPU revenue in the set is Anthropic 5.0 GW x $11.5B x 0.7457 XPU share = 42,877.8 plus Google's own TPUs 25,000 = 67,877.8 (before the SemiAnalysis scale). The 8i Max is two 8i dies on one package with 384 GB (RCR Tech, src 145); with the set's xpu_margin formula (HBM at $12.2/GB x 1.1, src 127) its revenue per unit is 1.843x the 8i's. The set reads 'mostly' as two-thirds of the cut units and puts the Max at one-third of 8i-series units (judgment; RCR 2026-11-10: 'neither product is shipping yet'). The cut's revenue share is then 20% x (2/3 x 1.843 + 1/3) / (1/3 x 1.843 + 2/3) = 24.39%, or 16,554.9 of CY2027 XPU revenue. Unit check (2026-11-23 gate fix): the analyst's 1M at ~20% implies a ~5.0M-unit Broadcom 8i series in 2027; his 2026-11-16 survey (analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, relayed by China Times src 181 and FourWeekMBA src 182) puts all Google TPUs at 8-9M in 2027 with MediaTek at 45-50%, so Broadcom 4.0-4.95M, consistent at the top (UBS's May figure of 6.76M Broadcom TPUs, src 121, is overtaken by it). Over ~5.0M units the set's 67,877.8 pool is $13.58k a unit (8i $10.60k and Max $19.53k at the 1.843x premium and a one-third Max mix), and on that price units, price and the 20% agree: 1M units, two-thirds Max = 2/3 x 19.53 + 1/3 x 10.60 = $16.55B, 24.4% of the pool's revenue for 20% of its units, the booked 16,554.9. In units, at the pool price Anthropic's 42,877.8 is ~3.16M (~0.63M per GW); at the stated prices Google's own 25,000 is ~1.80M units (the 1M cut units, $16.55B, plus the remaining $8.45B as plain 8i at $10.60k, ~0.80M), so the cut takes 1M of Google's ~1.80M units, 56% of its units and 66% of its revenue (the cut is mostly Max). The 66% is therefore the analyst's 20% of the whole series landing on Google's own fleet only (Anthropic's Broadcom leases are 'non-cancellable by either party except in the case of a default', Reuters, src 140; the page names neither the 8i nor 2027, so tying Anthropic's 2027 8i to those leases is the set's inference), not a sizing error. The set's Epoch-based $15.56-16.53k a unit (src 123) does not fit the analyst's ~5.0M units: 5.0M x $16.53k = $82.7B of 8i XPU revenue alone, above the ~$66.0B of TPU XPU revenue left in management's ~$115B FY27 outlook after OpenAI and Meta ((115 - 2.3 GW x 11.5) x 0.7457); the units x $16.53k and units x Max-price builds stay sized alternatives. Cross-check, CEO Hock Tan's 'multi-tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually' (src 38): Broadcom's 2027 TPU XPU revenue after the cut is 67,877.8 - 16,554.9 = 51,322.9 (Google-designed TPUs for Google and Anthropic), still multi-tens of billions; Google's own fleet alone falls to 8,445.1 before the SemiAnalysis scale, below it if the phrase meant Google's own purchases (the 2026-12-09 call can settle it). Timing (Broadcom's fiscal year runs Nov-Oct): CY2027 is phased by month on unit weights (the Max two-thirds of the cut units, the 8i one-third; by revenue the Max is ~79% of the cut, and revenue weights would put 73.3% of CY2027 in FY27 instead of 74.8%, ~$250M later; flat phasing is a sized alternative). The builds below assume 36 GB HBM4 stacks (576 GB) and that v9's non-memory value is twice 8i's for twice the compute dies (the set's estimate). judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: SemiAnalysis's Nov 13 Accelerator & HBM Model update (paywalled; read through two relays) cuts Broadcom's cumulative 2026-30 ASIC revenue by 11%, 'mainly due to average selling price adjustments from lower HBM costs rather than large-scale shipment reductions' (Tiger relay) and 'largely driven by price deflation rather than volume collapse', with Broadcom 'largely insulated' (456X relay). Our set builds AI revenue as customer GW x $11.5B per GW, with HBM resold at ~10% margin inside XPU revenue. The owner picked 'Volume net of moratorium' (card 2026-11-17 9:38 AM ET): the set books it as a volume cut on all AI revenue (XPUs and networking) net of the moratorium overlap, ai_rev x 0.89 / (1 - (1 - hs_self_funded) x dc_mor) in FY27-FY29, with Q1 FY27 (two-thirds calendar 2026, which SemiAnalysis left 'essentially unchanged') taking a third of it; xpu_share and xpu_margin are unchanged. This reads against the relays' price-led wording, by the owner's choice. It is a call because the relays give no per-year split and no price/volume split, and the primary note cannot be read.

options.reasoning: Both relays say the Broadcom cut is mainly lower HBM prices, not fewer chips; HBM is resold at a thin margin, so lower HBM prices cut revenue much more than profit (XPU EBIT -2% for -11% XPU revenue). GW stay on the company's Q3 FY26 call figures, and dc_mor keeps the delay risk.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: How should AVGO book the analyst's Google TPU cut after the v9 reconciliation?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International Securities) posted on 2026-11-20 that his industry survey shows Google cutting 2027 shipments of the Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series by ~1M units (~20%, 'mostly the higher-priced 8i Max / Whalefish'), shifting toward the MediaTek-designed 8t (https://stockanalysis.com/news/broadcom-falls-google-tpu-cut-mediatek/); AVGO fell 12.2% close to close (346.65 -> 304.41). Neither Google nor Broadcom has commented; consensus EPS is unrevised. 2027 is booked ground-up: $16.55B of CY2027 XPU revenue on Google's own fleet (1M of a ~5.0M-unit Broadcom 8i series at the pool's $13.58k a unit, mostly-Max units at $19.53k), networking held, 74.8% in FY27. What changed (your 11-23 request to reconcile Kuo and TrendForce): the two reports agree once the parts are named. TrendForce 2026-10-19 (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/10/19/news-mediateks-google-tpu-v9-shipments-may-slip-to-1q28-asic-race-heats-up-as-taiwan-firms-eye-new-opportunities/, relaying Commercial Times citing institutional investors) has 'revisions to Google's TPU v9 Core A design, codenamed Humufish' 'affecting the Core B and I/O designs handled by MediaTek'; TrendForce 2026-10-22 (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/10/22/breaking-google-reportedly-sticks-with-intel-emib-t-despite-35-substrate-yields-as-humufish-schedule-tightens/, industry sources) calls Core A a 'Google-designed Compute Die A, built on TSMC's N2' and lists the v9 lineup as 'Broadcom-designed WhaleFish, and MediaTek-designed HumuFish and TriggerFish' (WhaleFish on CoWoS-L, mass production 2H27; HumuFish 1H28; TriggerFish 2H28 or later). Kuo's cut is 'mostly the higher-priced 8i Max / Whalefish', so TrendForce's Broadcom WhaleFish and Kuo's 8i Max are the same Broadcom part, named v9 by one and 8i series by the other, and it is the part being cut. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo's (TF International Securities) 2026-11-16 survey (ChainCatcher https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2305019; China Times https://wantrich.chinatimes.com/news/20261117900182-420101) has MediaTek 'the sole design supplier for v9 (Humufish and Triggerfish)', v9 Google's main self-built compute from 2028, and 'due to initial capacity constraints, the main shipments until 2029 will still be from the v8 series', with v8 orders from OpenAI (~12M 8t) and Anthropic (~14M Broadcom 8i) over 2028-29; that leaves Broadcom's ~6.9M / ~7.2M 2028 / 2029 units at about Anthropic's ~7M a year, and ~4.5M for Google's own fleet, in line with Kuo's June Humufish lifecycle of 4-5M plus 1-2M Triggerfish (TechNews https://cdn.technews.tw/2026/06/23/google-and-mediatek-deepen-tpu-v9-collaboration-with-upgraded-triggerfish/). No source gives Broadcom Humufish or Triggerfish; Broadcom's 2026-04-06 8-K long-term agreement for 'Google's future generations of TPUs' (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/AVGO/8-k-broadcom-inc-reports-material-event-35aab0650b17.html) names no generation and is met by WhaleFish, so it stays the evidence for networking and the downside-protection side. Booked now: Google's own Broadcom TPU line ($25B a year of XPU revenue) gone from January 2028, Broadcom keeping what is left of WhaleFish / 8i Max and the 8i for Anthropic: FY28 cut 24.9B, FY29 25.0B (was half of Google's own v9 at MediaTek, 18.9B / 12.5B, the middle of reports then read as conflicting: now 378.11, +2.60%). Research target (12m) 368.53 vs 379.30 before the reconciliation and 407.73 before the Kuo update. Broadcom's FY28 TPU XPU revenue is then Anthropic's ~$75.0B, still 'multi-tens of billions' (CEO Hock Tan, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/09/broadcom-avgo-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Consequence for your 11-16 xpu_margin pick (v9 HBM4, half of FY28): Broadcom ships no Humufish, so the step has no Broadcom v9 part under it; the 8i-level margin is sized on that card. It is a call because the survey is unconfirmed and the Dec 9 call is the first company word. Update 2026-11-23 (owner picks): you booked this reading and set xpu_margin FY28-29 at the 8i level (55.90%) on the same reconciliation; with xpu_share on the 8i HBM share Broadcom's FY28 / FY29 TPU XPU revenue is Anthropic's 8.5 GW x $11.5B x 0.7457 = ~$72.9B a year before the SemiAnalysis scale. disagreements.topic: Discount rate for the DCF leg
disagreements.positions: agent_1 11.0% (5.31% + 5.7pt, judgment); agent_2 10.5% (my round-1 figure, 5.31% + 5.2pt, unsourced); agent_3 10.8% (5.31% + 5.5pt, judgment); agent_4 11.3% WACC (5.31% + 1.48 x 4.20%, 3.2% debt weight); agent_5 12.0% (5.31% + 1.48 x 4.5%, ERP judgment). disagreements.resolution: 11.5% cost of equity, applied to every DCF leg: 10-year Treasury 5.31% (2026-10-05) + 5-year beta 1.48 x Damodaran implied ERP 4.20% (2026-10-01, 'Trailing 12 month, with adjusted payout') = 11.53%. Cost of equity, not WACC, because every agent's DCF discounts FCF per share after interest (equity cash flow). Re-run at 11.5%, the agents' DCF legs are $315 / $280 / $284 / $291 / $291 (from $335 / $318 / $310 / $291 / $275) and their blended FVs become $409 / $414 / $387 / $407 / $389 (mean $401). My round-1 DCF ($338 at 10.5%) falls to $293. The rate explains most of the gap between agent 5 ($382) and the others; agent 5's remaining gap is its 0.4 DCF weight and 4.5% ERP.
disagreements.evidence: Treasury par curve CSV, 10/05/2026 10 Yr 5.31 (opened). Damodaran home page: implied ERP on October 1, 2026 'Implied ERP on October 1, 2026 = 4.20% (Trailing 12 month, with adjusted payout)' (US treasury rate 5.29%) (opened). disagreements.topic: FY28 AI semiconductor revenue anchor ($175-184B) vs the house capex input and the 10-Q purchase commitments
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $180B; agent_2 $180B (band $166-185B); agent_3 $175B; agent_4 $184B (230 x 0.8); agent_5 $177B (mean of $140.9B / $159.3B / $230B). Management: 'line of sight ... to again double to $230 billion. Here again, we have secured the supply'.
disagreements.resolution: Keep $180B as the base; the agents' range is consistent with both inputs, but it is not the conservative end. Mechanical anchors: constant share of house base capex 0.0625 x $2,255B = $141B; purchase commitments FY28/FY27 72,952/52,674 = 1.385 x $115B = $159B (AI-only) or $166B (semis-only, agent 2). $180B is 8.0% of 2028 base capex vs 6.2% in 2027, i.e. a +1.8pt share gain carried by the GW roadmap (Anthropic +5 GW in 2027 and +10 GW in 2028; OpenAI 1.3 GW and >5 GW). Two points weaken the 'commitments are still filling in' argument: the FY28 bucket was flat over the quarter ($72,870M at 2026-05-03 vs $72,952M at 2026-08-02) while FY27 fell ($55,214M -> $52,674M).
